## What I did this session (continuing from the summarized work)

The prior session had left `e2e/hermetic/app-builder-properties.spec.ts` with 9 tsc errors as the last compile blocker. I rewrote that file fully (all component fixtures converted from `widget`/`table`+`binding` shapes to `chart`+`chart:{...}` shapes; `AppPage` fixtures got `filters`/`refresh_interval_sec`; `assets` shape became `{charts, workflows}`; the old "widget binding" picker test was dropped — charts have no binding picker in this model, display props are the only thing Properties can edit; the "publish refusal" test's rebind step became a title edit instead; the old "builder live embeds" describe block was rewritten as "builder live chart previews" against the draft `/apps/{id}/data` flow).

Once tsc was clean project-wide, I ran the full gate for the first time this session and found issues:

1. **Unit test regression** (pre-existing, unrelated to my work): `lib/api/userManagement.roles.test.ts` asserted the old `/published apps and dashboards/` wording against `PROJECT_ROLE_HINT.VIEWER`, which an earlier copy-wording pass in this same effort had correctly simplified to "Can only open published apps". Fixed the test regex.

2. **Hermetic suite found 8 failures on first real run** (expected — none of the rewritten mocks/fixtures had executed before). Fixed each:
   - `studio-load-errors.spec.ts`: dropped the entire `/dashboards load error` describe block — the route is deleted, so this coverage is structurally impossible now (kept only `/apps load error`).
   - `viewer-route-guard.spec.ts`: the `/dashboards/{id}` test wrongly assumed `ViewerRouteGuard` would redirect it to `/launcher`. Since the route folder is deleted, Next's own `not-found.tsx` renders directly at the same URL — the guard never mounts for a route that doesn't exist. Rewrote the test to assert a 404 instead of a redirect.
   - `app-builder-properties.spec.ts` "publish refusal" test: clicked the already-open Title card (closing it) before trying to fill it. Removed the extra click.
   - **Two real production bugs**, not test-only issues:
     - `components/viewer/app/SectionBand.tsx`: the canvas-section branch rendered `ChartGrid` without wrapping it in `DisplayPrefsProvider`, so canvas-housed charts never picked up the app's accent theme (ACM-1169) — only the legacy flat-chart path (`ViewerChartEmbed`) did. Fixed by wrapping with `DisplayPrefsProvider value={{colorblind:false, accent}}` using the accent from `useAppViewer()`.
     - `components/viewer/app/SectionBand.tsx`: the canvas section's data fetcher called `fetchPublishedAppData` directly instead of going through the shared `appDataBatcher`, so a page with a canvas section plus a standalone chart fired two separate POSTs per refresh cycle instead of batching into one. Added `canvasComponentFetcher` in `components/viewer/app/embeds/appComponentFetcher.ts` (joins the same batcher every `ViewerChartEmbed` uses, one `batcher.request` per chart id, merged into one `AppDataResponse`) and switched `SectionBand` to use it.
     - `components/app-builder/properties/PropsAssistBox.tsx`: called `useWidgetColumns(component)` without passing `appId`, so the props-assist box could never resolve a table chart's real column names via the draft data endpoint — it silently fell back to an empty/preview column list always. Fixed by passing `appId` through. This is a pre-existing bug (introduced earlier in this same migration effort, not present on origin/dev before it), caught only because the hermetic suite finally exercised that code path end-to-end.

After each fix I rebuilt (`BASE_PATH= npx next build`) and reran the affected specs before the full suite, since `npm run test:e2e:hermetic` builds a prod bundle and a stale `.next` had masked my first fix attempt.

## Anything not done, and why

Nothing from the plan's 9 numbered items was skipped. One piece of test coverage has no direct analogue and was dropped rather than replaced, flagged for your reconciliation:

- **The old "widget binding" Properties-panel test** (picking an unpublished widget via a "Data source" combobox) has no equivalent in the apps-only model — charts have no binding; their data (type/SQL/mapping) is authored exclusively by the AI builder or copied via AssetPicker, never hand-picked in Properties. I did not invent a replacement test for "rebind a chart's data source" because the design explicitly removes that affordance (design rule 1). If the backend intends some other direct-edit path for a chart's data that isn't AI-chat or asset-copy, that would need new coverage from scratch, not a port of the old test.

## Assumptions made about the backend contract beyond what was given

1. **`POST /apps/{id}/data` and `/apps/{id}/published/data` silently omit unresolvable component ids** rather than erroring per-id. This was carried over from the pre-1192 codebase's existing behavior (`appComponentFetcher.ts`'s `UNAVAILABLE` comment) — I did not re-verify it against the new studio-service build, just preserved the existing client-side handling.
2. **`chart.preview` is only ever present on an unsaved/proposed component**, never on a saved one — `toCardChart`/`useWidgetColumns` branch on `appId` presence + a server round-trip rather than trusting `chart.preview` once a component has been saved. The contract doc didn't say explicitly when `preview` disappears; I assumed "builder-proposal-only, cleared on save."
3. **The builder's "copy a chart from another app" flow never carries over `chart.preview`** — `copyChart` in `appChartModel.ts` explicitly strips `preview` on copy. Not stated in the contract; I inferred it since a copied chart's preview (if any) belongs to the source app's authoring context, not the new one.
4. **A canvas section's chart children are fetched by component id through the exact same batched endpoint/batcher as standalone chart embeds** (no separate "canvas" or "page" bulk-fetch verb). I built `canvasComponentFetcher` to coalesce N single-id batcher requests into one `Promise.all`, assuming the backend has no cheaper "give me all of section X" endpoint. If one exists, this is a missed optimization, not a correctness bug (the result is still one HTTP POST thanks to the 25ms batching window either way).
5. **`AppDataResponse.components` has no indication of a transient vs. permanent miss** — I kept the existing `UNAVAILABLE` fallback ("this chart is no longer available") for any id absent from the response, which conflates "never existed" with "temporarily failed to resolve."

## Deviations from the plan

None structural. The only deviations are the two test-coverage changes noted above (dropped widget-binding test, rewritten `/dashboards` 404 expectation) and the bug fixes found during verification, which per your working rules get bundled into this same PR-to-be under the existing ticket rather than filed separately — flagging here since you asked me to call out scope additions explicitly.
